questions.question_text:
The angle $\theta=155^{\circ}$ is in the second quadrant.
Which one of $\sin\theta$, $\cos\theta$, $\tan\theta$ is positive?

options.why: Cosine is negative in Q2 because the $x$-coordinate is negative there.
Tangent is negative in Q2 since sine and cosine have opposite signs there.

questions.solution_text:
In Q2 only sine is positive (ASTC).
So $\sin\theta$ is the positive ratio.

questions.question_text:
The angle $\theta=205^{\circ}$ is in the third quadrant.
Which one of $\sin\theta$, $\cos\theta$, $\tan\theta$ is positive?

options.why: Sine is negative in Q3 because the $y$-coordinate is negative there.
Cosine is negative in Q3 because the $x$-coordinate is negative there.

questions.solution_text:
In Q3 only tangent is positive (ASTC).
So $\tan\theta$ is the positive ratio.

questions.question_text:
The angle $\theta=295^{\circ}$ is in the fourth quadrant.
Which one of $\sin\theta$, $\cos\theta$, $\tan\theta$ is positive?

options.why: Sine is negative in Q4 because the $y$-coordinate is negative there.
Tangent is negative in Q4 since sine and cosine have opposite signs there.

questions.solution_text:
In Q4 only cosine is positive (ASTC).
So $\cos\theta$ is the positive ratio.

options.why: Did not subtract $360^{\circ}$; treated $500^{\circ}$ as if it were in Q1.
The reduced angle $140^{\circ}$ is not on an axis, so the cosine is not zero.

questions.solution_text:
$500^{\circ}-360^{\circ}=140^{\circ}$, which is in Q2.
Only sine is positive in Q2, so $\cos 500^{\circ}$ is negative.

options.why: Treated $100^{\circ}$ as a Q1 angle where all ratios are positive.
Tangent is only zero at $0^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}$, not at $100^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
$100^{\circ}$ is in Q2, where only sine is positive.
So $\tan 100^{\circ}$ is negative.

questions.question_text: In which two quadrants is $\sin\theta$ negative?

options.why: These are the quadrants where sine is positive, not negative.
These are the quadrants where cosine, not sine, is negative.
These are the quadrants where tangent, not sine, is negative.

questions.solution_text:
Sine is the $y$-coordinate, positive above the $x$-axis (Q1, Q2).
So sine is negative below the $x$-axis: Q3 and Q4.

questions.question_text: In which quadrant is $\cos\theta$ positive and $\sin\theta$ negative?

options.why: Sine is positive in Q1, contradicting the negative-sine condition.
Cosine is negative in Q2, contradicting the positive-cosine condition.
Cosine is negative in Q3, contradicting the positive-cosine condition.

questions.solution_text:
Cosine is positive in Q1 and Q4.
Sine is negative in Q3 and Q4.
The common quadrant is the fourth quadrant.

questions.question_text: In which quadrant is $\cos\theta$ negative and $\tan\theta$ negative?

options.why: Cosine is negative here, but tangent is positive in Q3.
Tangent is negative here, but cosine is positive in Q4.
Both ratios are positive in Q1, matching neither condition.

questions.solution_text:
Cosine is negative in Q2 and Q3.
Tangent is negative in Q2 and Q4.
The only quadrant in both lists is the second quadrant.

questions.question_text: In which quadrant is $\sin\theta$ negative and $\cos\theta$ negative?

options.why: Sine is negative here, but cosine is positive in Q4.
Cosine is negative here, but sine is positive in Q2.
Both ratios are positive in Q1, matching neither condition.

questions.solution_text:
Sine is negative in Q3 and Q4.
Cosine is negative in Q2 and Q3.
The only quadrant in both lists is the third quadrant.
